items.title: Negroni Sbagliato
items.subtitle: A happy accident
items.description: Born from a bartender's mistake in Milan, prosecco replaces gin for a lighter, effervescent twist on the classic Negroni. Bittersweet, floral, and impossibly elegant.

items.title: Penicillin
items.subtitle: Smoky medicine
items.description: Created by Sam Ross at Milk & Honey NYC. A blend of blended Scotch with honey-ginger syrup, fresh lemon, and a float of peaty Islay whisky. Modern classic status achieved.

items.title: Jungle Bird
items.subtitle: Bitter tropical escape
items.description: A Kuala Lumpur hotel original that spent decades in obscurity before becoming a cult favourite. Dark rum meets Campari, pineapple and lime in a perfectly balanced bittersweet tiki drink.

items.title: Paper Plane
items.subtitle: Equal parts perfection
items.description: Sam Ross strikes again. Equal parts bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino and fresh lemon juice. A cocktail of mathematical elegance that somehow tastes greater than the sum of its parts.

items.title: Naked & Famous
items.subtitle: Desert rose
items.description: A southwest US riff on the Paper Plane using mezcal instead of bourbon. Smoky, floral with Aperol and Yellow Chartreuse. Joaquín Simó's masterpiece from Death & Co.

items.title: Toronto
items.subtitle: The thinking person's Manhattan
items.description: Rye whisky and Fernet-Branca in perfect harmony, softened by simple syrup and aromatic bitters. Complex, herbal and deeply satisfying. The cocktail for someone who says they don't like cocktails.

items.title: Gimlet
items.subtitle: Gin & lime, forever
items.description: Originally made with preserved lime juice by the British Royal Navy, the modern gimlet with fresh lime and a touch of cordial is a study in simplicity. Clean, tart, and beautifully green.

items.title: Oaxacan Old Fashioned
items.subtitle: Smoke meets agave
items.description: Phil Ward's game-changing recipe from Death & Co splits the base between tequila and mezcal, adding mole bitters and agave syrup. Redefined what a split-base cocktail could be.

items.title: Clover Club
items.subtitle: Velvet & raspberry
items.description: A pre-Prohibition classic from Philadelphia's gentleman's clubs. Gin, fresh lemon, raspberry syrup and egg white shaken until silky. Pink, pillowy, and utterly sophisticated.

items.title: Last Word
items.subtitle: Prohibition survivor
items.description: Equal parts gin, green Chartreuse, maraschino liqueur and lime juice. Forgotten for decades and revived by Murray Stenson in Seattle circa 2004. Now one of the most ordered cocktails worldwide.

items.title: Bees Knees
items.subtitle: Honey & sunshine
items.description: Born during Prohibition to mask the harsh taste of bathtub gin. Honey syrup and fresh lemon juice elevated cheap spirit into something genuinely delightful. We kept the recipe; improved the gin.

items.title: Corpse Reviver #2
items.subtitle: Hair of the dog, refined
items.description: A pick-me-up from the Savoy Cocktail Book. Gin, Cointreau, Lillet Blanc and lemon with a rinse of absinthe.
